comment: Opt-in heterogeneous review panel. Activate with SCIFORGE_PROVIDERS=kernel/config/providers.heterogeneous.example.json (copy it first and fill in real endpoints). The shipped providers.json stays single-backend so a box with one credential keeps working; this file exists because a panel whose three personas and chair all resolve to one model reports homogeneous_degraded, and its spread then measures sampling noise rather than reviewer disagreement. Requirements: (1) each reviewer persona must use a DIFFERENT role, and those roles must map to different backend/model pairs - giving two personas the same role gives them the same model no matter how many personas you declare; (2) adjudication must differ from every reviewer role, otherwise the chair adjudicates its own disagreement (adjudicator_distinct=false); (3) set protocol explicitly when a backend speaks Anthropic but is not named 'anthropic' - name-only inference sends it to /chat/completions and it 404s; (4) pinned:true exempts a role from the SCIFORGE_MODEL host override, which would otherwise flatten the panel back onto one model. Verify with: python -c "from sciforge.providers import Providers; from sciforge.review import panel_independence, _default_personas; p=Providers(); print(panel_independence(p, _default_personas(p)))" - expect status=heterogeneous, distinct_models>=2, adjudicator_distinct=true. Endpoints below are placeholders: a gateway that routes by provider id needs one backend entry per provider, each with its own base_url.
personas_note: review._default_personas assigns role='review' to all three lenses. To spread them across backends, pass explicit personas to review_paper, e.g. [{'id':'methods','role':'review',...},{'id':'novelty','role':'reasoning',...},{'id':'repro','role':'grading',...}]. Declaring more personas without varying the role does not create model independence.
